slides.title: Test the Action. Before It Reaches a Customer.
slides.subtitle: Cora Recap Engine  ·  an operational AI system
slides.caption: A system calls an admissions team's leads, texts and emails them, and writes what happened into their record.

slides.title: Each of those actions has a consequence.
slides.subtitle: A call reaches a person. A text lands on a phone. A changed field changes what the team does next.
slides.caption: A model that writes a convincing message can still attach it to the wrong lead, the wrong campaign or the wrong moment.

slides.title: Two gates, at the boundary.
slides.subtitle: One for calls, texts and emails. A separate one for writes to the CRM.
slides.caption: Every job still runs and every message is still written. Only the last step is held, and what is held is written down.
Both gates reading shadow, with every change to them listed underneath. This copy runs on this machine with no keys, which is why the pre-flight list shows errors.
One lead's held run: four actions recorded, two messages stored, and no call events at all, because a held call is never placed. Every row here is a placeholder.
Each step of that run is marked shadow, and the text the model wrote is there to read in full.

rows: intended actions recorded instead of performed in five days
kept the exact words or fields they would have sent
mode changes, each with its old value, new value and source
slides.caption: Read from the system's own tables: in five days of rehearsal, 4,267 intended actions for 722 leads were held, and 3,204 of them kept their words or fields.

slides.title: The rehearsal ran beside the old workflow.
slides.subtitle: 717 of the 721 leads it would have called were being called by the workflow it was replacing.
slides.caption: Nothing pairs a real call with the one it shadowed. The overlap and the go-live runbook are what the record rests on.

slides.title: What a rehearsal cannot prove.
slides.subtitle: No completion event. No recorded review. No evaluation of the words.
slides.caption: A held call produces no completion, so nothing after it happens. Nothing records that a person read a held action. And none of the six evaluations of the model's call summaries ran with a fixture.

slides.title: Going live was two audited changes, six seconds apart.
slides.subtitle: 18 April 2026, 12:41 AM Central.
slides.caption: Both gates opened from that one page, each change recorded with its old value, its new value and where it came from.
